evidence.field: 字形演變; 金文索引
evidence.text: The database records a bronze inscription form of 是 under 集成02724 and lists the transmitted small-seal form under 說文. The page offers no oracle-bone form for this character. The indexed form supports an attested bronze graph, but the accessible text does not explain its original referent or components.
evidence.title: 漢字「是」：字形演變

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明
evidence.text: The dictionary reproduces the Shuowen account: 是 means 直, and is analyzed as 从日、正; it also gives the received Zhou-script form as 从古文正. It describes the regular-script lower portion as a changed form of 正 and explicitly distinguishes it from 疋. This is evidence for the traditional seal-form analysis, not proof that the earlier bronze graph originally consisted of 日 and 正.
evidence.title: [A01791] 是 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Lin Deng, Bulletin of Chinese Linguistics (article abstract hosted by ResearchGate)
evidence.field: Abstract; early uses and proposed source
evidence.text: Deng analyzes bronze-inscription 是 from the Western Zhou through the Warring States period and compares it with the received Odes and Documents. The abstract reports early pronominal, anaphoric and focus-marking uses, and proposes a possible morphological relationship to 之 in focus position. It says a connection to 唯 remains speculative. This is a linguistic account of the word and its use, not an explanation of the graph's visual components.
evidence.title: Some New Insight into the Historical Source of the Chinese Copula Shì/*deʔ 是

evidence.source: Silpakorn University Journal of the Faculty of Arts
evidence.text: The article describes a development from demonstrative pronoun, through a demonstrative with copula-like properties, to copula use during the Eastern Han period. It reports that zero-copula and verbal-copula constructions continued in parallel, with copula constructions increasing substantially after the Tang and replacing the zero-copula pattern in modern narrative after the May Fourth Movement. These are the article's periodization claims; the abstract does not supply individual dated examples.
evidence.title: Development of "是" Copula Verb and Copula Construction in Chinese

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary separates senses including 'straight', 'right/correct' opposite 非, demonstrative 'this', connective uses, object-fronting constructions, and affirmative response. It cites examples from works such as the Analects, Mencius, Huainanzi, and Hou Hanshu. These citations establish examples within the cited works, but the page does not date the composition or manuscript witness of each example; they should not be treated as a precise chronology of semantic change.
evidence.title: [A01791] 是 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The entry identifies the character as U+662F and indexes bronze form 集成02724. The accessible page lists no oracle-bone item; its instructions say the database displays oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript and Shuowen small-seal materials where available, omitting unavailable material. This supports recording a bronze attestation and an absence in this database, not a claim that no oracle-bone form exists anywhere.
evidence.title: 漢字「是」：字形演變

search_audit.outcome: The Deng article abstract was inspected and provides a scholarly analysis of early bronze-inscription pronominal uses and a qualified proposal about relation to 之. Ctext and KCI pages could not be opened; no individual inscription text or dated literary example was verified in this search.

gaps: The original graphic referent and motivation of the earliest reported bronze form are unresolved in the inspected primary-facing database. The traditional 日 plus 正 analysis is specifically the Shuowen seal-form analysis; the dossier's inferred 日 plus 𤴓 account and the popular explanations involving a sundial, arrow, key, or graphic corruption were not independently established here.
No visual glyph image was inspected. The Academia Sinica page indexes 集成02724 but does not expose a textual reading of its shape in the page content available to this research.

The character-specific Unicode Unihan URL https://www.unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=662F timed out, and the component record attempt for U+65E5 was inaccessible. The supplied local Unihan row gives 是 kMandarin shì; no phonetic-component claim is made, so a modern component/host sound comparison is not applicable. Do not cite the local row as external evidence without an accessible official record.

The supplied local Baxter–Sagart row for 是 is MC dzyeX and OC *[d]eʔ, gloss 'this'. It was checked as supplied input but the local file is not an external source URL and no official upstream table page was inspected. It supports no claim about the graph's components or an independent phonetic element.

The evidence distinguishes claims about the word from claims about the graph. The proposed relationship of early 是 to 之 is a morphological/linguistic hypothesis, not evidence that the whole graph 是 was borrowed to write a separate homophonous word. A source-word/object borrowing account was not found or required by the inspected analyses.

No independently verified earliest attestation of a copula example, or dated earliest attestation of the 'right/correct' sense, was collected. The Eastern Han date for copula function is an article's summary claim; the dictionary's cited examples do not alone establish semantic chronology.

Deng's full article was unavailable on the inspected ResearchGate page. Its abstract says the link from 是 to 唯 is speculative, but its detailed inscription inventory and argument could not be checked.
